title: The J-2 property passes from an affine open cover to every affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open covering. If every ring $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is J-2, then for every affine open $V\subseteq X$ the ring $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is J-2. Here J-2 is the ring predicate of [def-exc-excellent-ring]: the regular locus of every finite type algebra over the ring is open.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), implication (4) implies (3). The S in the printed covering formula in (4) denotes the scheme X of the lemma.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$, and let $R\to B$ be any finite type algebra. Apply [lem-trf-affine-test-algebra-chart-refinement] to $X,(U_i),V,B$. It gives a Noetherian $R$, a locally Noetherian $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the locally finite type composite $f:Y\to X$, and affine opens $W_y$ covering $Y$ with $f(W_y)\subseteq U_{i(y)}$ and finite type maps $A_y=\mathcal O_X(U_{i(y)})\to C_y=\mathcal O_Y(W_y)$.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof of (4) implies (1) and (1) implies (3), specialized directly to an arbitrary finite type algebra over the chosen affine open.; assembly of the two separated arguments.

proof.text: For each $y$, the hypothesis says $A_y$ is J-2. Its defining clause [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to the finite type $A_y$-algebra $C_y$, makes $E(C_y)=\{\mathfrak q:(C_y)_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ open. The affine-cover criterion in [lem-trf-regular-locus-affine-chart-gluing], applied to this locally Noetherian $Y$ and the cover $(W_y)$, now gives openness of $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$. The criterion includes an empty $Y$ and uses no finite subcover.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof of (4) implies (1) and (1) implies (3), specialized directly to an arbitrary finite type algebra over the chosen affine open.; assembly of the two separated arguments.

proof.text: The whole affine $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an affine open of the locally Noetherian $Y$, so [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $B$ Noetherian. The last clause of [lem-trf-regular-locus-affine-chart-gluing] identifies the open $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$ with $E(B)$. Thus every finite type $R$-algebra has open regular locus. By the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], $R$ is J-2. Both $B$ and $V$ were arbitrary, proving the statement.
